articles.title: Uefa investigating allegation Israel player spat at Ireland coach
articles.summary: Allegation of an incident in or near tunnel at half-time. Israeli FA denies anyone spat ‘towards the coach’ Uefa has launched an investigation into claims a member of the Republic of Ireland coaching staff was spat at during the heated Nations League encounter with Israel on Sunday.
body: The European governing body has confirmed that post-match reports submitted by match officials “contained an allegation of an incident in or around the tunnel at half-time” and that it will be the subject of a disciplinary investigation “regarding potential misconducts from player(s)”.

Witnesses at the match, held in the Serbian town of Backa Topola, reported hearing a member of the Irish staff – understood to be the fitness coach Damian Doyle – claim he had been spat on by an Israeli player as the teams went down the tunnel at half-time.
A spokesperson for the Israeli Football Association denied the reports, saying “no one had spat towards the coach”.
After the match Ireland’s coach, Heimir Hallgrímsson, said his team had been subject to a number of apparent provocations in the buildup and sought to defuse the incident.

articles.title: Deion Sanders created Prime Time so he could get paid. Why deny college athletes the same chance?
articles.summary: The Hall of Famer says his successful college career helped him and his family thrive. Now he appears to be backing legislation that would help others. Last week, journalist Rob Parker called Deion Sanders a “sellout” for taking part in an advert promoting the Protect College Sports Act (PCSA).
body: The major points of contention around the PCSA, which the Senate passed last week and now awaits approval from the House, are a ceiling of around $49m that schools can direct to athletes, as well as a new transfer rule that would, except in a few specific circumstances, restrict players to one “free” transfer (if they move schools again, they’d have to wait a year to play for their next team). Former NFL player Domonique Foxworth has said that “the core of [the PCSA] is about reestablishing the power the NCAA had in the past – that the court system determined was illegal”.

Sanders takes a different approach. In his pro-PCSA ad, he notes, “As a coach and father, I’m helping the next generation find their spotlight. That’s why I support the Protect College Sports Act. It gives student-athletes a chance to shine on and off the field, strengthens historically Black colleges and universities, and keeps both men’s and women’s sports strong.”

articles.title: Uefa investigating Republic of Ireland-Israel row after spitting accusation
articles.summary: Uefa has confirms it is investigating the half-time incident during Sunday's Nations League game between Republic of Ireland and Israel following an accusation of spitting.
body: The teams clashed at half-time in the 1-1 draw behind closed doors in Serbia, with the Irish Times, external reporting that Republic of Ireland head of athletic performance Damien Doyle alleged he had been spat at by an Israel player.
Republic of Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later confirmed there was an "accusation of spitting" during the fracas.
On Tuesday, Uefa confirmed it was opening an investigation "following a review of the official reports".

"An Uefa Ethics and Disciplinary Inspector has been appointed to conduct the appropriate disciplinary investigation regarding potential misconducts from player(s) on the occasion of the Uefa Nations League 2027 League Phase match between Republic of Ireland and Israel, played on 4 October 2026 in Backa Topola, Serbia," added European football's governing body.

articles.title: ‘I will not be moving on’: sale of WNBA’s Connecticut Sun leaves Native fans facing cultural loss
articles.summary: The Mohegan Tribe made the Sun the first Native American-owned franchise in pro sports. Fans say the team’s move to Houston echoes centuries of erasure and displacement.
body: When the Connecticut Sun played their final WNBA game last month, fans at Mohegan Sun Arena came together in an act of collective celebration and grief. The beloved franchise was leaving after 24 seasons, sold to a new ownership group in Houston, in a process so controversial that the state of Connecticut is considering legal action. The end of the Sun is a loss for the entire New England region, which is now without a WNBA team.

The Sun entered the league in 2003 and brought professional women’s basketball to Connecticut, which is considered the “Basketball Capital of the World” – at least, according to signs along the state’s highways. The Sun were the first independently owned WNBA team, and the first Native American-owned pro sports franchise.

The story of the Mohegan Tribe, which bought the Sun in 2003, often gets lost in conversations about the team. But it shouldn’t, Native fans told the Guardian. You can’t understand the birth or the death of the team without understanding Native history and the ways cultural and historical harm still reverberates today.

articles.title: ‘Brighton are the world’s most forward-thinking club’: Jason McCarthy on retiring at 29 to coach
articles.summary: Former Wycombe defender thought he might end up becoming a pastor but stayed in the game he loves. “You blow your whistle and then, all of a sudden, voom, you have 20, 30 people standing to attention,” says Jason McCarthy, discussing his transition into coaching after retiring from playing aged 29.
body: He accepted the role of Brighton’s under-21s assistant at the start of last year and recently returned to the role after two months in interim charge this summer, while the head coach, Shannon Ruth, supported Fabian Hürzeler’s first-team staff. McCarthy has huge admiration for Hürzeler, Brighton’s impressive 33-year-old head coach who at 31 became the youngest permanent manager in Premier League history and was part of his interview process.

Brighton, third in the top flight before visiting Sunderland on Saturday after a flying start, are frequently referenced as a model club. McCarthy chuckles as a moment that speaks to Hürzeler’s “incredible growth mindset” crosses his mind. “I saw him running around the training ground, holding a piece of paper and reading. I think he read somewhere that taking on information while exercising can help you remember it. He’s constantly trying to improve himself. How can you not be inspired by that?”

articles.title: Cheetahs to play European games in Swansea
articles.summary: South African side Cheetahs will play their European Challenge Cup home matches this season at St Helen's in Swansea, the home of Welsh side Ospreys.
body: Cheetahs host Dragons on Sunday, 13 December and Perpignan on Sunday, 17 January with both games a day after Ospreys' home matches in the same competition.
Cheetahs have traditionally used Europe as a base for matches in the second-tier tournament, with games in the 2025-26 season taking place in Amsterdam.

There are links between Ospreys and Cheetahs. Y11 Sports & Media owns a majority stake in the Ospreys and maintain an investment interest in the South African team with players moving between both sides.
The Ospreys' first game at the redeveloped St Helen's is scheduled to be the United Rugby Championship (URC) Welsh derby against Dragons on Saturday, 24 October.

articles.title: Donley keen to add goals after encouraging NI run
articles.summary: After a four-game window with plenty of positives for Northern Ireland, there was perhaps just one lingering concern - their ability to score goals consistently.
body: Tottenham Hotspur's Jamie Donley started as a lone striker throughout the quartet of Nations League fixtures, even though the 21-year-old has stated he feels his more natural position is number 10.

Despite impressing with his ability to push Northern Ireland up the field, drop into space, frustrate the opposition and, as a result, win plenty of free-kicks, he failed to add to his two international goals across the window where his side won twice but were frustrated in a pair of goalless home draws.

Spearheading the attack for a young side who have already proven they are hard to break down at the other end, Donley's failure to score despite playing 294 minutes across the four games will be cause for concern.
"I've enjoyed it, playing all four games," said the player on loan at Luton Town.

articles.title: Scotland vs Slovenia – Match preview and team news
articles.summary: Scotland will look to end this international break on a high when they host Slovenia at the Barclays Hampden in Glasgow on Tuesday in their fourth UEFA Nations league group fixture. Scotland vs Slovenia – Match preview and team news. Date: Tuesday, 6th October. Kick-off: 7:45pm BST.
body: Scotland head coach Sébastien Pocognoli faces an enforced defensive reshuffle ahead of their crucial UEFA Nations League tie at Hampden Park.
Central defender Scott McKenna is completely ruled out of the squad following a late red card picked up during the team’s 2-0 victory against North Macedonia.

In a massive boost to the backline, fellow centre-back Jack Hendry returns to availability after serving his own one-match suspension. However, the hosts remain significantly depleted in the attacking and midfield departments.
Reliable forward Che Adams and striker Lawrence Shankland are both sidelined with ongoing injuries, while midfield star Scott McTominay is unavailable following a recent medical procedure.

body: Croatia enters their upcoming fixture seeking a vital response under manager Slaven Bilić following a tough defeat against England.

The squad faces several forced adjustments, particularly in defence, as centre-back Martin Erlić remains sidelined with an injury until mid-October, and right-back Josip Juranović is unavailable due to illness.
These absences will force a reshuffle in the backline, where Josip Šutalo is heavily tipped to return to the starting eleven to restore defensive stability.

articles.title: Russell set for Singapore GP grid penalty after engine failure
articles.summary: George Russell is set to start from the back of the grid at Sunday's Singapore Grand Prix due to a power unit change in a further blow to his championship hopes.
body: Russell suffered a power unit failure late in Sunday's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia when running third, forcing him to retire while his Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli finished second to extend his lead over the Brit at the top of the Drivers' Championship to 84 points with seven rounds remaining.

Sky Sports News understands Russell will take on a new power unit on Friday in Singapore, which will see him exceed the season allocation of four for each driver, therefore incurring a penalty that will drop him to the rear of the grid.

Russell was expected to have a new power unit at the United States Grand Prix later this month that was going to include an upgrade, with Mercedes taking up the opportunity they were granted by the FIA's ADUO (Additional Development and Upgrade Opportunities) system to improve their engine.

The ranking of Mercedes' engine performance below Red Bull's by the sport's governing body has caused some dispute, with the Milton Keynes squad arguing that the Silver Arrows, who are dominating the Constructors' Championship, already have the best power unit.

articles.title: World No 1 Sinner to miss rest of 2026 season
articles.summary: World No 1 ‌Jannik Sinner will miss the rest of the 2026 season due to the knee injury that has kept him on the sidelines since winning Wimbledon.
body: Speaking in a video message on social media, the Italian said: "Me, together with the doctors, have decided that I need a course of treatment for my knee, which means that the 2026 season is officially over.

"The last couple of years gave me so many beautiful feelings and emotions, which this year is going to be way different, but I also need to think about my long-term career so I will do everything possible to get back 100 per cent.
"I will thank you already in advance for your support and hope to see you very, very soon on court again. Ciao ciao!"
Sinner's team added in a statement: "On the advice ​of his ⁠medical team, Jannik ⁠Sinner will follow a course ‌of treatment for inflammation in his knee.
